blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the distinction between marginal and effective tax thinking shapes the quality of every decision. The marginal rate is the tax rate on the next pound of taxable income — the one that matters when evaluating a new project, a price increase, or an additional hire. The effective rate is the average rate across the whole year — the one that matters for investor communication, budgeting, and benchmarking.

Senior leaders who confuse the two reach the wrong conclusion on almost every decision. A project priced at the effective rate looks healthier than it really is; a budget built on the marginal rate looks tighter than it really is. Both mistakes are quiet and persistent.

The discipline at this level is to ask, for every tax conversation, which rate the question actually calls for. It sounds pedantic. It is, at senior level, one of the simplest ways to avoid thousands of pounds of unnecessary confusion.

items.q: According to the text, which rate matters when evaluating a new project or an additional hire?
items.why: "The marginal rate is the tax rate on the next pound… the one that matters when evaluating a new project… or an additional hire."

items.q: Why does a project priced at the effective rate look "healthier than it really is"?
options: The effective rate is usually lower than the marginal rate on the next pound of income
The effective rate is set by investors, not by policy
The effective rate double-counts the year's costs
The effective rate ignores revenue entirely
items.why: Inferência: a decisão incremental é tributada à marginal (mais alta); usar a efetiva (média, menor) infla a atratividade do projeto.

items.q: The author describes both mistakes as "quiet and persistent." This most likely suggests that…
options: they go unnoticed and keep distorting decisions over time
they cancel each other out in the end
they are easy to spot and quick to correct
items.why: Inferência: "quiet" = passam despercebidos; "persistent" = seguem distorcendo — logo, não se corrigem sozinhos.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Asking which rate a question calls for is worth the effort.
The effective rate is the right lens for benchmarking.
Confusing the two rates leads to the wrong conclusion.
One rate can serve equally well for both budgeting and pricing the next hire.
items.why: Inferência: toda a tese é que cada pergunta exige a alíquota certa — uma única alíquota não serve para os dois usos.

items.q: Why does the author concede that the discipline "sounds pedantic"?
options: To warn that it wastes time in meetings
To acknowledge the objection, then argue the payoff outweighs it
To admit the distinction has no practical value
To suggest only auditors should worry about it
items.why: Inferência: ele antecipa a crítica ("pedante") só para rebatê-la — evita milhares de libras de confusão.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry orientando o novo executivo depois da apresentação do projeto. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Sit down for a second — the deck was clean, and I want to flag one thing before it becomes a habit. You priced the project at the effective rate. That's the average across the year, and it made the return look better than it is.

The decision you were actually putting to the board was incremental. Do we take on this contract? Do we make this hire? The money at stake is the next pound of profit, and the next pound is taxed at the marginal rate — which, for us, sits well above the average. So the real return is thinner than the slide claimed.

I'm not accusing anyone of dressing up the numbers. It's an easy slip, and honestly it's persistent — I've watched sharp people make it for years. But once it's in a board pack, it drives capital the wrong way.

Here's the habit I want. Before any tax figure goes on a slide, ask one question: is this decision about the margin or about the average? Marginal for a go or no-go; effective for budgeting and the investor story. Get that right and nobody downstream inherits a quiet mistake.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What mistake did the executive make in the deck?
options: He applied a foreign tax rate by mistake
He left the tax rate off the slide entirely
He priced the project at the effective rate instead of the marginal rate
items.why: "You priced the project at the effective rate… it made the return look better than it is."

items.q: Why does Harry say the marginal rate is the right one for this decision?
options: Because the marginal rate is lower for the company
Because the board prefers marginal figures
Because effective rates are illegal in board packs
Because the decision is incremental — the money at stake is the next pound of profit
items.why: "The decision… was incremental… the next pound is taxed at the marginal rate."

items.q: What does Harry mean when he says "nobody downstream inherits a quiet mistake"?
options: The board never reads the appendix
The error would spread to later decisions if it went uncorrected
The mistake would be caught by the auditors anyway
The junior staff would be blamed for it
items.why: Inferência: uma vez no board pack, o erro "silencioso" contamina decisões de capital seguintes.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's attitude toward the executive?
options: Coaching and reassuring, while still correcting the substance
items.why: Inferência: "I'm not accusing anyone… it's an easy slip" — ele corrige, mas protege e ensina.

items.q: According to Harry, which rate belongs in the investor story and the budget?
options: A blended rate agreed with the board
Whichever rate is higher that year
items.why: "Marginal for a go or no-go; effective for budgeting and the investor story."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "On this hire, the marginal rate is what erodes the return." The marginal rate is…
options: the tax rate applied to the next pound of taxable income
the lowest rate in the schedule
the average tax paid across the whole year
items.why: Marginal rate = alíquota marginal: o imposto sobre o próximo libra ganho.

items.q: "For the annual report, quote the effective rate." The effective rate is…
options: the average rate borne across the entire year
the rate on the last unit of income
items.why: Effective rate = alíquota efetiva: a média do imposto sobre o ano todo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The error was small each quarter but ___ — it never went away."
items.why: Persistent = persistente: continua ao longo do tempo, sem se corrigir.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We use ___ to see how our margins compare against peers in the sector."
items.why: Benchmarking = comparação com referências de mercado ou concorrentes.

items.q: "The distinction sounds pedantic, yet it saves real money." Pedantic here means…
options: excessively concerned with tiny, formal details
items.why: Pedantic = pedante: preso a minúcias formais — aqui, o autor admite a crítica só para rebatê-la.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de finanças e decisão executiva. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the pricing assumptions." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Using the effective rate here would flatter the return." To flatter the numbers means to…
options: make them look better than they truly are
round them to the nearest thousand
items.why: To flatter the numbers = fazê-los parecer melhores do que são — exatamente o risco da alíquota efetiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the tax figure in the deck." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "That correction won't move the needle on the headline return." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.

items.q: "Let's not gloss over which rate the decision actually calls for." To gloss over means to…
options: treat something briefly to hide its importance
items.why: Gloss over = passar por cima, tratar de leve para disfarçar a relevância.
